name: Mitochondrial non-syndromic hearing loss (MT-RNR1 aminoglycoside sensitivity)

clinicalPearls: Maternally inherited variants in the mitochondrial genome, classically m.1555A>G in MT-RNR1, predispose to sensorineural hearing loss
Affected individuals are exquisitely susceptible to aminoglycoside ototoxicity, which can trigger severe irreversible loss even after a single standard course
Baseline hearing may be normal, mild, or progressive, and susceptibility can be silent until an aminoglycoside is given
The pattern of maternal transmission with no father-to-child inheritance is a key pedigree clue
Genotype knowledge allows aminoglycoside avoidance across an entire maternal lineage, a highly preventable cause of deafness
Rapid point-of-care or pre-prescription testing is increasingly used to avoid ototoxic exposure in acute settings
MT-TS1 variants such as m.7445A>G are additional maternally inherited causes
reference.pathophysiology: The mitochondrial 12S ribosomal RNA gene MT-RNR1 forms part of the mitochondrial ribosome. The m.1555A>G variant alters the RNA so that it more closely resembles the bacterial ribosomal binding site targeted by aminoglycosides, increasing drug binding and impairing mitochondrial protein synthesis. Because cochlear hair cells are highly dependent on oxidative metabolism, this susceptibility renders them vulnerable to aminoglycoside-induced injury, producing sensorineural hearing loss. Even without drug exposure some carriers develop progressive loss, reflecting a milder underlying deficit in mitochondrial function; the mitochondrial genome is inherited exclusively through the maternal line, explaining the pattern of transmission.
additionalDifferentials: Non-mitochondrial hereditary sensorineural hearing loss (DFNA and DFNB)
Acquired aminoglycoside ototoxicity without a predisposing variant
Syndromic mitochondrial disease with additional systemic features
additionalInvestigations: Pure-tone audiometry to establish baseline thresholds and monitor progression
Otoacoustic emissions and brainstem response to characterise cochlear function
Mitochondrial genetic testing for m.1555A>G and related MT-RNR1 and MT-TS1 variants
Detailed maternal-lineage pedigree to identify at-risk relatives
Review of prior and planned aminoglycoside exposure
Assessment for wider mitochondrial disease when systemic features are present
redFlags: Planned or ongoing aminoglycoside therapy in a person with the variant or a suggestive maternal history
Sudden severe hearing loss following aminoglycoside exposure
Systemic features suggesting a broader mitochondrial disorder
reference.prognosis: Aminoglycoside-triggered loss is typically severe and irreversible, but the disorder is highly preventable through drug avoidance; baseline and progressive loss are managed with amplification or cochlear implantation.
pitfalls: Prescribing an aminoglycoside without eliciting a maternal deafness history or checking genotype where feasible
Assuming ototoxicity requires prolonged high exposure when a single course can suffice in carriers
Failing to warn and test maternal relatives after diagnosis
Overlooking the diagnosis in progressive loss with a maternal inheritance pattern
references: GeneReviews: Mitochondrial Nonsyndromic Hearing Loss and Deafness
